regime_context: Canada/TSX shows a broad (88% eligible), non-narrow rotation with Gold Miners as the clear leader (score 2.167, durability 0.85, full breadth) but with a healthy challenger margin and absorption of only 0.31 — so leadership is emphatic but not a crowded one-narrative blow-off. The absolute-trend gate has historically helped on this market (gate_helps=true), so anchoring to eligible trend-health is the one leg with a real risk edge; rank remains an attention lens only.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Silver & Royalties closes the 0.552 margin against Gold Miners with its own durability bar (0.77) holding above 0.7 and a full breadth reading — that would suggest a confirmed broadening of the precious-metals narrative beyond gold alone; if instead Silver's durability slips below 0.6 while Gold holds 0.85, I retire the watch and treat Gold Miners as the sole PM vehicle.

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners are the dominant eligible narrative with the strongest rank, highest durability (0.85), full breadth (1.0), and a persistent 'trend' Hurst tag — the staying-power leg is the strongest signal in the whole state. Crowding is not flagged (z=0.95, crowded=false), so this is leadership without blow-off texture. As the only theme where trend-gate eligibility, breadth and durability all align, it deserves the lean while the absolute-trend gate stays on.
evidence: durability_bar 0.85 — highest of all scorable themes
theses.dissent: The rotate margin is wide but absorption is low, and macro_narrative shows AI/geopolitics dominating headlines — not gold-specific news. If this is a legacy reflation play rather than a fresh safe-haven bid, the leadership could stall without a catalyst. Also, track_record dir_accuracy of 0.302 is poor — past directional leans have been unreliable.

falsifier.text: XGD.TO falls below its 50-day level or Gold Miners' durability_bar drops below 0.5 before the check-by date

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals rank 3rd but carries the only crowding flag in the top half (crowding_z=1.23, crowded=true) alongside a 'mixed' Hurst tag. Per the guardrails, crowding is a size-down caution only — so this is a lean to avoid/size-down, not a fade. The theme is eligible and mid-ranked but its flow texture is the least clean among the leaders.
evidence: crowded=true, crowding_z=1.23 — the highest crowding z in the table
rank #3 but with the only top-half crowding flag
theses.dissent: Copper and base metals can run independently on physical supply tightness rather than financial flow, and 'mixed' trend does not mean the uptrend is broken. Avoiding it could mean missing a legitimate reflation leg.

falsifier.text: XBM.TO makes a new 20-day high while crowded=true persists, and base metals' breadth stays 1.0

theses.subject: REITs
theses.thesis: REITs sit at the bottom of the eligible ladder with zero breadth (0.0), a 'mixed' Hurst tag, and deeply negative score (-1.08). The absolute-trend gate's risk edge argues against holding bottom-decile breadth in a rate-sensitive sector unless a clear new trend forms. This is a de-risk/avoid lean, not a short.
theses.dissent: REITs are rate-sensitive and could snap back on any Bank of Canada dovish shift; zero breadth also means expectations are already floor-level from a sentiment standpoint.

falsifier.text: XRE.TO rises more than 8% with breadth recovering above 0.5
